sentences.text: Shargaotis is an extinct bird genus placed in the bustard family Otididae.
Only a single species, Shargaotis ignipes, is known, represented by a fragment of the lower leg bone called the tibiotarsus.
Morphologically it most closely resembles the living bustard genera Otis and Chlamydotis.
Fossils were recovered from the Sharga locality in western Mongolia, an area exposing Miocene rock layers.
The material was collected during Soviet-Russian-Mongolian paleontological expeditions in 1978, 1979, 1984 and 2001.
The holotype, the specimen on which the species is based, is curated at the Paleontological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences under accession PIN 4869/249.
The generic name combines the locality name Sharga with Otis, the name of the great bustard, while the specific epithet ignipes translates as “fiery-footed” or “extremely fast”.
Additional bustard fragments from the same site include a distal left tibiotarsus and a wing-finger base phalanx, both catalogued separately.
The formal description was released online in 2026, bearing a printed issue date of December 2025.
The genus lived in the Middle Miocene of Mongolia.
Some researchers propose that two further bustard fragments, which resemble Chlamydotis, could belong to Shargaotis, but they remain classified as indeterminate.
